title: Bay Area storm timeline: Rain returns, bringing potentially dangerous surf along coast, several inches of snow to the Sierra
text:
Bay Area storm timeline: Rain returns, bringing potentially dangerous surf along coast, several inches of snow to the Sierra - ABC7 San Francisco 
 24/7 Live San Francisco East Bay South Bay Peninsula North Bay WEATHER 
 Level 2 storm to bring rain, dangerous surf to Bay Area and more than a foot of snow to the Sierra 
 Rain is expected to return to the region Friday, bringing potentially dangerous surf along the coast and snow to the Sierra. By Drew Tuma , Gloria Rodríguez Thursday, November 12, 2026 1:25AM Share SAN FRANCISCO (KGO) -- Rain is expected to return to the Bay Area on Friday, bringing gusty winds, dangerous surf and the first accumulating snowstorm of the season to the Sierra.
 ABC7 meteorologist Drew Tuma says the system has been upgraded to a Level 2 storm, the first moderate storm of the season, and is expected to bring an end to the region's fire season.
 Most Bay Area cities are forecast to receive about a half-inch of rain, with higher amounts possible in the North Bay and Santa Cruz Mountains. Rainfall totals are expected to range from 0.50 to more than 1.5 inches, accompanied by wind gusts of 30 to 50 mph.
 The heaviest rain and strongest winds are expected between 10 a.m. and 2 p.m. Friday, with showers continuing into the afternoon and a chance of thunderstorms.
 Along the coast, forecasters are warning of increasingly dangerous conditions as surf builds through Friday. A Beach Hazards Statement remains in effect through Friday afternoon, while a High Surf Warning has been issued as waves of 20 to 30 feet are expected to slam Bay Area beaches through Saturday.
 Rain is expected to return to the region Friday, bringing potentially dangerous surf along the coast and snow to the Sierra.

 "The water's getting aggressive. It's growing. The swell is increasing," Pacifica surfer Craig Garza said.
 Large waves were already visible at Pacifica's Linda Mar Beach and San Francisco's Ocean Beach, with surf expected to increase throughout the week. Experienced surfers are urging beachgoers to use caution and stay away from the water's edge, especially with the threat of sneaker waves.
 "Don't let your kids out anywhere near the water. These tides will suck them kids right out. It's dangerous," surfer Curtis Wedge said.
 Garza warned that conditions can change rapidly.
 "It could look flat. It could look calm. And then all of a sudden, here comes 3 or 4 giant waves, and they push way up high on shore. And if you're not careful, you'll get pulled out," he said.
 Officials say sneaker waves can arrive without warning and sweep people into the ocean, even when conditions appear calm.
 In the Sierra, the storm is expected to bring the first accumulating snowfall of the season. Forecasters predict 6 to 12 inches of snow at lake level, with more than 18 inches possible at the highest elevations.
